title: Generating useful background images
author: Odd-Sympathy-9556
selftext:
Hi everyone! First time posting here and I come for assistance.

Since the rise of vibe coding, I finally gained ~~courage~~ time to start working on an iOS game (I work full time as an iOS engineer).

The gif shows a bit of my combat scene, unfinished and very much unpolished. As context, I have a grid of 2 columns with 4 rows across (2 teams, left and right).  
  
Here's my problem though, doesn't matter what I try, I simply cannot create an usable background image for the combat scene. I've tried midjourney, dabbling around with ComfyUI, NanoBanana and many other platforms/tools but I always end up with an image, that despite having the theme and style accurate for what I want, it never matches the camera or the layout that I need, in order to place my units (ground them).

I've also tried to use the coding agents which deeply understand the positioning of the combat, to provide me with prompts I can use to create such assets. Also failed miserably. I had tons of ideas for scenary that I could use depending on where the comabt happens but can't even get past the first hurdle of having an image that actual fits the perspective.

Does anyone have any ideas now how I can achieve such a thing to at least remove this hideous gray background?

comments.author: kytheon
comments.body: To make something good with AI, you need to understand what you want to make. Only then you can properly prompt. In this case it would be a very specific camera view, probably Orthographic Top Down.

comments.author: DreamNotDeferred
comments.body:
Try prompting with a focus on NES/SNES-era Final Fantasy battle-style backgrounds. Feed some images of combat from those games, and tell the AI you want that camera angle.

Also, did you use AI for your character sprites? If so, would you mind sharing your workflow? They're cool.

https://preview.redd.it/k3w69awdtdcg1.jpeg?width=2736&format=pjpg&auto=webp&s=6f853ed84f70dc8e30a9bff818b082948fb3661f

replies.author: Odd-Sympathy-9556
replies.body:
Thanks! That’s actual a great idea!

Yes, I did. I used Midjourney to get the overall concept and looks of the character. Then I used nano banana to make edits (clothing, weapons, face, you name it). For some I still edited with photoshop a bit but most are still is desperate need of cleaning up. Finally, I uploaded to ludo.ai and used it to create the pose and the sprite animations.

replies.author: DreamNotDeferred
replies.body: Thanks for sharing. Keep us posted on how your development is going, and let us see the backgrounds when you get some.

comments.author: agarlington
comments.body: I have a handful of tools I could throw at you/suggest and highly recommend for retro 2d pixel art stylization. my personal top workflow picks, all gonna be paid though such as any AI subscription.

comments.author: frankleelife
comments.body: Actually you can use Gemini, chatgpt, I also tried to use SceneOF ai, which is specially for generating culturally adapted images. Depends on what you need.
